name: Security Scan

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 2 * * 1' # Weekly on Monday at 2 AM UTC
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  audit:
    name: Dependency Audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    
    - name: Install Rust
      uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
    
    - name: Install cargo-audit
      run: cargo install cargo-audit
    
    - name: Run cargo audit
      run: cargo audit --json > audit-results.json
      working-directory: ./roshera-backend
      continue-on-error: true
    
    - name: Upload audit results
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
      with:
        name: security-audit
        path: roshera-backend/audit-results.json

  license-check:
    name: License Compliance
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    
    - name: Install Rust
      uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
    
    - name: Install cargo-license
      run: cargo install cargo-license
    
    - name: Check licenses
      run: |
        cargo license --json > licenses.json
        # Check for GPL/AGPL licenses that could affect commercial use
        if grep -E '"license":\s*"(A?GPL|LGPL)"' licenses.json; then
          echo "::error::GPL/AGPL license detected - commercial risk"
          exit 1
        fi
      working-directory: ./roshera-backend

  secrets-scan:
    name: Secrets Detection
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        fetch-depth: 0
    
    - name: Run secret detection
      uses: trufflesecurity/trufflehog@main
      with:
        path: ./
        # For push events, compare against previous commit to avoid scanning the same commit twice
        base: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.event.before || 'main' }}
        head: HEAD
        extra_args: --debug --only-verified

name: CI/CD Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, develop, 'fix/**', 'feat/**' ]
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main ]

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1
  # Debuginfo for the 190+ test binaries exceeds runner disk (killed run 29547226449
  # with "No space left on device"); same no-debuginfo discipline as local dev.
  CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: "false"
  CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG: "false"

jobs:
  test:
    name: Test Suite
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Link every crate + the ~100 integration-test binaries with mold instead
    # of GNU ld. Linking (each test binary statically links the large
    # geometry-engine rlib) was the dominant cost of the cold build; mold is
    # 5-10x faster, which is what brings a cold build back inside the timeout.
    env:
      RUSTFLAGS: "-C link-arg=-fuse-ld=mold"
    # Bound a hung or runaway test run instead of GitHub's 6h default. A single
    # deadlocked test (e.g. the verify_api_key DashMap self-deadlock) would
    # otherwise burn the entire 6h job limit before being cancelled.
    #
    # 60 min (not 30): the cargo cache had gone cold (LRU-evicted while CI was
    # red on the fmt gate for days), so the workspace + every test binary must
    # compile from scratch — that alone is ~30-40 min on the 2-core runner,
    # plus the nextest run. A 30-min cap was cancelled before the build even
    # finished, so the cache never SAVED and every run stayed cold. This higher
    # cap lets one cold run complete and warm the cache; warm runs finish in
    # ~10-15 min (revisit/lower this once green is observed).
    timeout-minutes: 60

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Free disk space
      # The optimized test/dev profile produces larger artifacts; on a cold
      # (cache-miss) build the workspace + all deps + every nextest binary
      # overran the runner's ~14 GB root disk ("No space left on device").
      # Remove the preinstalled toolchains we don't use (~25-30 GB) up front.
      run: |
        sudo rm -rf /usr/local/lib/android /usr/share/dotnet /opt/ghc \
          /opt/hostedtoolcache/CodeQL /usr/local/share/boost \
          /usr/local/lib/node_modules 2>/dev/null || true
        sudo docker image prune -af 2>/dev/null || true
        df -h /

    - name: Install system dependencies
      run: |
        sudo apt-get update
        sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config mold

    - name: Install Rust
      uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      with:
        components: rustfmt, clippy

    - name: Cache cargo dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: |
          ~/.cargo/registry
          ~/.cargo/git
          target
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-cargo-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}

    - name: Enforce API-only AI provider policy (no local models)
      # CLAUDE.md mandates hosted-API providers only. This guard fails the
      # build if Ollama / LLaMA / Whisper / Candle identifiers are
      # reintroduced into the Rust backend or config files.
      run: |
        set -e
        PATTERN='\b(ollama|llama|whisper|candle)\b'
        # Scope: Rust sources, Cargo manifests, and config files under roshera-backend/.
        # Exclude generated indexes, docs, and legacy markdown.
        MATCHES=$(grep -RInE "$PATTERN" \
          --include='*.rs' --include='*.toml' --include='*.yaml' --include='*.yml' \
          roshera-backend/ \
          | grep -viE '^[^:]+:[^:]+:\s*(//|#).*' \
          || true)
        if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
          echo "::error::Forbidden local-model identifiers found (API-only policy):"
          echo "$MATCHES"
          exit 1
        fi

    - name: Check formatting
      run: cargo fmt --all -- --check
      working-directory: ./roshera-backend
    
    - name: Run clippy
      # Clippy's own exit code is authoritative: nonzero on any error-level
      # lint (incl. the workspace's denied unwrap/expect/panic), zero on
      # warnings. The old `| tee | (! grep 'error\[E')` pipeline (no pipefail)
      # swallowed clippy lint failures — only numbered rustc errors tripped it.
      run: cargo clippy --all-targets --workspace
      working-directory: ./roshera-backend

    - name: Install cargo-nextest
      uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
      with:
        tool: nextest

    - name: Run tests (nextest)
      # nextest runs each test in its own process under a work-stealing
      # scheduler — substantially faster than libtest on a suite this size and
      # it prints a clean per-test failure summary. --no-fail-fast surfaces
      # every failing crate in one run; a slow/hung test is reported and the
      # 40 min job timeout bounds the cost. nextest does NOT execute doctests,
      # so they run separately afterwards.
      run: |
        # Full workspace in parallel. (timeline-engine was briefly run isolated
        # + single-threaded to dodge an intermittent hang; that hang — a
        # create_branch DashMap shard self-deadlock — is now fixed, so it runs
        # with everything else again. The slow-timeout in .config/nextest.toml
        # remains as a backstop for any future hang.) Doctests last (nextest
        # does not run them).
        cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast
        cargo test --workspace --doc --no-fail-fast
      working-directory: ./roshera-backend

    - name: Run kernel demo regression suite
      # Each demo asserts non-zero triangle counts and bbox invariants on
      # outputs from primitives, booleans, extrude/revolve, sweep/loft,
      # features, transforms, and pattern/draft. A regression in any of these
      # paths fails CI loudly. See plans/steady-sauteeing-nova.md Phase 3
      # ("demos become regression tests"). (demo_extrude_revolve and
      # demo_sweep_loft were each excluded while their pre-existing
      # revolve/loft non-manifold bugs were fixed; both now build valid
      # watertight-topology solids and are back in the gate.)
      run: |
        set -e
        for demo in demo_primitives demo_booleans demo_extrude_revolve \
                    demo_sweep_loft demo_features demo_transforms \
                    demo_pattern_draft; do
          echo "==> $demo"
          cargo run --release --example "$demo" -p geometry-engine
        done
      working-directory: ./roshera-backend

    # Benchmarks not yet implemented
    # - name: Run benchmarks (dry run)
    #   run: cargo bench --no-run
    #   working-directory: ./roshera-backend

  frontend:
    name: Frontend Build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Setup Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '20'
        cache: 'npm'
        cache-dependency-path: roshera-app/package-lock.json

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci
      working-directory: ./roshera-app

    - name: Type check
      run: npx tsc -b
      working-directory: ./roshera-app

    - name: Lint
      run: npm run lint
      working-directory: ./roshera-app

    - name: Build
      run: npm run build
      working-directory: ./roshera-app

  rl-harness:
    # `roshera-rl` runs certificate-scored agent episodes over the MCP surface
    # and projects the resulting JSONL trajectories into Postgres. It had NO CI
    # job at all until now — its suites ran only when a human typed `npm test`.
    #
    # That is the same defect this workflow just fixed for the constraint-gate
    # suites, one package over, and it bites harder here: this package holds the
    # parity test pinning its copy of `MUTATES_SOLIDS` to `gates.ts`'s. An
    # unrun parity test is not a pin, and `gates.ts` gained mutating verbs twice
    # in a single branch.
    #
    # Triggered by changes to EITHER package, because a `gates.ts` edit is
    # exactly what the parity test exists to catch and `roshera-rl/**` alone
    # would miss it.
    #
    # A Postgres service DOES run here, and the reasoning that said otherwise
    # is superseded rather than deleted, because the change of mind is the
    # useful part. When this job was written the argument was: the ingest suite
    # states an honest reasoned skip without a database, the rest is offline,
    # and turning one honest skip into a run is a later call. That was true.
    #
    # It stopped being true the moment the branch put load-bearing coverage
    # INSIDE the skipped block. `rl_episode.unverified_mutations` — the column
    # that answers "which episodes ended with mutating work nobody verified" —
    # has exactly one real round-trip test, and it sits in the block that
    # skips. So the honest skip had quietly become the thing hiding the only
    # proof that the migration works, and a skip that hides load-bearing
    # coverage is no longer honest, however well it explains itself.
    #
    # The suite still passes with no database and still states its skip, so
    # nothing here depends on the service being reachable to be correct — the
    # service exists to stop one specific test from never running.
    name: RL harness (episode + trajectory + parity)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:16
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: roshera
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        # Without the health check the job can reach `npm test` before Postgres
        # accepts connections, and the suite would take its honest skip — going
        # green while proving exactly what it was proving before the service
        # was added. A flaky skip is worse than a stated one.
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Detect roshera-rl or gates.ts changes
      uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
      id: filter
      with:
        filters: |
          rl:
            - 'roshera-rl/**'
            - 'roshera-mcp/src/gates.ts'

    - name: Setup Node.js
      if: steps.filter.outputs.rl == 'true'
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '20'
        cache: 'npm'
        cache-dependency-path: roshera-rl/package-lock.json

    - name: Install dependencies
      if: steps.filter.outputs.rl == 'true'
      run: npm ci
      working-directory: ./roshera-rl

    # One invocation, not two: the suite is the test AND the evidence.
    #
    # The second half matters as much as the first. The suite SKIPS its ingest
    # tests when it cannot reach a database and reports that honestly rather
    # than failing — right locally, and exactly the wrong thing to rely on
    # here, because a service that silently stopped resolving would turn this
    # job green while testing strictly less than it did the day before. The
    # whole reason the service was added is that one test must actually run,
    # so a skip is a failure in this environment even though it is a virtue
    # outside it. `pipefail` so npm's own exit code still decides the step.
    #
    # The assertion is POSITIVE — "this suite reported passing checks" — not a
    # grep for the skip message, which is how it was first written and was a
    # guard that FAILED OPEN on its two likeliest decay paths: reword that
    # message in `ingest_store.test.mjs`, or drop the suite from the `test`
    # chain, and a negative grep finds nothing and the job goes green having
    # proved strictly less. That is the same defect this job exists to catch,
    # in the catcher. A positive anchor fails CLOSED on all three cases —
    # skipped, reworded, removed — because all three produce no success line.
    #
    # Anchored with `^…$` so it cannot match npm's own echo of the test chain,
    # which contains the substring `ingest_store` on its command line;
    # verified against real logs in both directions before being written here.
    - name: Run the RL harness suites (and refuse a silent no-database skip)
      if: steps.filter.outputs.rl == 'true'
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -o pipefail
        npm test 2>&1 | tee rl-test.log
        if ! grep -qE '^ingest_store: [0-9]+ checks passed$' rl-test.log; then
          echo "::error::ingest_store did not report a passing run. Either it took its no-database skip although a postgres service is configured, or it is no longer in the test chain. Either way the unverified_mutations migration round-trip did NOT run and this job proves less than it claims."
          exit 1
        fi
      working-directory: ./roshera-rl
      env:
        ROSHERA_RL_PG: postgresql://postgres:postgres@localhost:5432/roshera

  mcp-quality:
    # The jig ratchet (MCP scale architecture, Slice 5). Grades the agent tool
    # surface the way the fmt gate grades formatting: the minimal default surface
    # must stay under the token budget, every exposed param must be described
    # (schema hygiene = 100), and no tool may balloon past the per-tool ceiling.
    # Runs only when roshera-mcp/** changes (dorny/paths-filter, keeping the
    # existing whole-workflow push/PR triggers untouched).
    name: MCP Quality (jig ratchet)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Detect roshera-mcp changes
      uses: dorny/paths-filter@v3
      id: filter
      with:
        filters: |
          mcp:
            - 'roshera-mcp/**'
            # ontology_coverage.mjs (test:drift) parses this file for the
            # MCP<->backend bench-parity check. b4231410 changed ONLY this
            # file and turned that test red, unseen by an mcp-only filter.
            - 'roshera-backend/api-server/src/agent_registry.rs'

    - name: Setup Node.js
      if: steps.filter.outputs.mcp == 'true'
      uses: actions/setup-node@v4
      with:
        node-version: '20'
        cache: 'npm'
        cache-dependency-path: roshera-mcp/package-lock.json

    - name: Setup Python
      if: steps.filter.outputs.mcp == 'true'
      uses: actions/setup-python@v5
      with:
        python-version: '3.12'

    - name: Install dependencies + build dist
      if: steps.filter.outputs.mcp == 'true'
      run: |
        npm ci
        npm run build
      working-directory: ./roshera-mcp

    - name: Run MCP drift tests
      if: steps.filter.outputs.mcp == 'true'
      # `npm run test:drift` compiles src/ to test/.build and runs the four
      # suites that pin the tool SURFACE — fully offline, no backend:
      #   scale_s2.mjs          S2 invariants (table/minimal/full counts,
      #                         meta-tool validation parity, find_tool ranking,
      #                         TS<->Rust FNV-1a-64 registry hash, bill < 8000)
      #   kb_lookup.mjs         the exact resident token bill + kb_lookup's
      #                         reference/provenance contract
      #   find_tool_heldout.mjs held-out find_tool recall ratchet floors
      #   ontology_coverage.mjs every tool benched, and MCP<->backend bench
      #                         parity against agent_registry.rs
      # Only scale_s2 ran here before, against dist/; the other three were in
      # no gate and all four sat red for weeks (audit Task 93). They read
      # test/.build, not dist/, so they measure the source being merged.
      #
      # test/auto_feedback.mjs is EXCLUDED on purpose: its STATIC half greps a
      # monolithic src/index.ts for per-tool server.tool() blocks + okp() /
      # perceive() / ROSHERA_MCP_AUTOVERIFY, but the S2 refactor split those out
      # of index.ts into per-domain tools/*.ts modules behind the ToolTable, so
      # those assertions are stale/red. It is tracked separately from this gate;
      # wiring it in here would fail CI on a known-stale test, not a regression.
      run: npm run test:drift
      working-directory: ./roshera-mcp

    - name: Run constraint-gate suites
      if: steps.filter.outputs.mcp == 'true'
      # The four suites that prove the CONSTRAINT harness — the refusal cache,
      # the intent gate, the unsound-base gate, the sheet-export gate, the
      # single-point-run gate and the verification-scope gate. Each has at
      # least one check that fails if its gate's logic is deleted (audited
      # 2026-08-14), so this step is a real gate rather than a smoke test.
      #
      # They ran nowhere until now: `scale_s2.mjs` above is the only MCP test
      # CI executed, and it mentions the intent gate only to work AROUND it.
      # The mutation proofs behind these suites were real history that nothing
      # re-established — which matters more since `roshera-rl` began treating
      # these gates as an RL environment's dynamics, where a refusal is a
      # training signal and a silently-removed gate corrupts a corpus.
      #
      # They compile src/ to test/.build (an untracked fixture, never dist/)
      # so every assertion runs the real ToolTable wrapper and the real
      # handlers against a stub backend — the exact path a live call takes,
      # minus the Rust kernel. `npm run test:gates` does that build itself.
      #
      # A FIFTH suite exists and deliberately does NOT run here:
      # `constraint_gates_live.mjs` drives the same gates against a REAL
      # running backend (:8081 or ROSHERA_URL), which CI does not have. It is
      # invocable as `npm run test:gates:live` — it was previously runnable by
      # no script at all, which is why it is named here rather than left to be
      # rediscovered.
      #
      # It is safe to leave out of CI precisely because it does not fake
      # success without a backend: its reachability probe exits **2** — a code
      # distinct from a test failure's 1, meaning "could not run" rather than
      # "ran and passed". An absent backend can therefore never be mistaken
      # for a green live pass. Run it by hand against a live server before
      # shipping gate changes; the four above cover the logic offline.
      run: npm run test:gates
      working-directory: ./roshera-mcp

    - name: Grade with jig (best-effort, non-blocking)
      if: steps.filter.outputs.mcp == 'true'
      # jig (github.com/Shodh-Labs/jig, the MCP report-card grader) is NOT
      # published to PyPI under a verifiable name: `pip install jig` resolves to
      # an UNRELATED git-hook framework (robmadole/jig), and `jig-mcp` does not
      # exist. So we attempt the real grader from its own source, verify the
      # installed CLI is actually the MCP grader (exposes `check`/`budget`), and
      # SKIP loudly otherwise — never mis-installing the PyPI shadow, never
      # failing CI on jig's absence. The fallback gate below is authoritative.
      continue-on-error: true
      run: |
        set +e
        NOTE() { echo "$1"; echo "$1" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"; }
        echo "## MCP jig grader" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
        pip install "jig @ git+https://github.com/Shodh-Labs/jig@v0.4.0" >/tmp/jig_install.log 2>&1
        if command -v jig >/dev/null 2>&1 && jig --help 2>&1 | grep -Eq '\bcheck\b|\bbudget\b'; then
          NOTE "jig grader installed ($(jig --version 2>&1 | head -1)) — running check + budget."
          jig check --stdio "node dist/index.js" || NOTE "jig check reported findings (see log; fallback gate is authoritative)."
          jig budget --json || NOTE "jig budget reported findings (see log; fallback gate is authoritative)."
        else
          NOTE ":information_source: jig MCP grader not installable on this runner (PyPI \`jig\` is an unrelated git-hook tool; \`jig-mcp\` does not exist; the Shodh-Labs source install did not yield a \`check\`/\`budget\` CLI). Relying on the authoritative fallback gate below."
        fi
      working-directory: ./roshera-mcp

    - name: MCP budget + hygiene gate (authoritative)
      if: steps.filter.outputs.mcp == 'true'
      # The always-run, gate-authoritative grader. Speaks minimal MCP stdio to
      # the built server on both ROSHERA_MCP_SURFACE=minimal and =full, then
      # asserts the spec §5 Q5 budgets: minimal live-surface bill <= 8000 tok,
      # schema hygiene = 100 (every param described), per-tool <= 3.5x full-set
      # median except the wire-contract-fixed allowlist. tiktoken (o200k_base)
      # when installable, else the registry's chars/4 estimate.
      run: |
        pip install tiktoken >/dev/null 2>&1 || echo "tiktoken unavailable — gate falls back to chars/4 (registry-parity)"
        python tools/mcp_budget_gate.py
      working-directory: ./roshera-mcp

  security:
    name: Security Audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    
    - name: Install system dependencies
      run: |
        sudo apt-get update
        sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config
    
    - name: Install Rust
      uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
    
    - name: Install cargo-audit
      run: cargo install cargo-audit
    
    - name: Run security audit
      run: cargo audit
      working-directory: ./roshera-backend
      continue-on-error: true

  benchmark:
    name: Run Benchmarks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    timeout-minutes: 45

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    
    - name: Install system dependencies
      run: |
        sudo apt-get update
        sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config
    
    - name: Install Rust
      uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
    
    - name: Cache cargo dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: |
          ~/.cargo/registry
          ~/.cargo/git
          target
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-bench-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}
    
    - name: Run benchmarks
      run: |
        # Run criterion benchmarks if they exist
        if cargo bench --workspace --no-run 2>/dev/null; then
          cargo bench --workspace -- --output-format bencher | tee bench-results.txt
        else
          echo "No benchmarks found, skipping"
        fi
      working-directory: ./roshera-backend

  performance:
    name: Performance Regression
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    timeout-minutes: 45

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        fetch-depth: 0
    
    - name: Install system dependencies
      run: |
        sudo apt-get update
        sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config
    
    - name: Install Rust
      uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
    
    - name: Cache cargo dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v3
      with:
        path: |
          ~/.cargo/registry
          ~/.cargo/git
          target
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-perf-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}
    
    - name: Install critcmp
      run: cargo install critcmp
    
    - name: Run benchmark baseline
      run: |
        git checkout ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        # Check if benchmark exists before running
        if cargo bench --bench geometry_bench --no-run 2>/dev/null; then
          cargo bench --bench geometry_bench -- --save-baseline main --output-format bencher | tee bench-results.json
        else
          echo "No benchmarks found in base branch"
          echo '{"results": []}' > bench-results.json
        fi
      working-directory: ./roshera-backend
    
    - name: Run benchmark comparison
      run: |
        git checkout ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        # Check if benchmark exists before running
        if cargo bench --bench geometry_bench --no-run 2>/dev/null; then
          cargo bench --bench geometry_bench -- --save-baseline pr --output-format bencher | tee bench-results.json
          if [ -d target/criterion/main ]; then
            critcmp main pr || echo "Benchmark comparison skipped"
          fi
        else
          echo "No benchmarks found in PR branch"
          echo '{"results": []}' > bench-results.json
        fi
      working-directory: ./roshera-backend

  deploy:
    name: Deploy (build + push images to GHCR)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [test, frontend, security]
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    timeout-minutes: 45

    # The built-in GITHUB_TOKEN needs packages:write to push to GHCR; contents
    # stays read for checkout. This replaces the old "build a release and upload
    # an artifact that deploys nowhere" job with two container images a partner
    # instance can actually pull (see docker-compose.partner.yml).
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write

    env:
      REGISTRY: ghcr.io
      BACKEND_IMAGE: ghcr.io/varun29ankus/roshera-cad
      FRONTEND_IMAGE: ghcr.io/varun29ankus/roshera-cad-frontend

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Log in to GHCR
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ${{ env.REGISTRY }}
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build and push backend image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
      with:
        context: ./roshera-backend
        file: ./roshera-backend/Dockerfile
        push: true
        tags: |
          ${{ env.BACKEND_IMAGE }}:${{ github.sha }}
          ${{ env.BACKEND_IMAGE }}:latest
        cache-from: type=gha
        cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

    - name: Build and push frontend image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v6
      with:
        context: ./roshera-app
        file: ./roshera-app/Dockerfile
        push: true
        tags: |
          ${{ env.FRONTEND_IMAGE }}:${{ github.sha }}
          ${{ env.FRONTEND_IMAGE }}:latest
        # The public WebSocket URL is a per-partner value set at deploy time in
        # docker-compose.partner.yml (PUBLIC_WS_URL); the published image ships
        # a relative /ws default that partner compose overrides on build.
        build-args: |
          VITE_API_URL=
          VITE_WS_URL=/ws
        cache-from: type=gha
        cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

# never reached goose's 0.13. Declaring 0.13 here puts us in ITS universe;

#

# chosen or every https:// request will fail at runtime." Slice 2 shipped,
# Sarvam became the first provider to use goose's HTTP client rather than
# spawning a CLI, and every turn failed. This is that choice, made.
reqwest_013_tls_for_goose = { package = "reqwest", version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["native-tls"] }

#
# - git dependency: the crates.io name `goose` is an unrelated load-testing
#   framework (tag1consulting/goose); the Block agent harness is not
#   published. Pinned to an explicit rev — never a floating branch.
# - default-features = false, NO feature list: goose's `default` feature set
#   is empty, but we state it explicitly so a future upstream default cannot
#   silently widen our build. Deliberately NO TLS feature either
#   (`native-tls` requires OpenSSL dev libs — absent on the Windows dev
#   host; `rustls-tls` drags in aws-lc-rs, which wants CMake/NASM). goose's
#   TLS features gate only (a) TLS termination for its own standalone
#   server — Roshera terminates its own connections — and (b) the HTTPS
#   backend of goose's outbound reqwest client. Slice 1 makes no outbound
#   call; before slice 2 sends live provider traffic through goose, a TLS
#   feature must be chosen or every https:// request will fail at runtime.

#   exist in this binary regardless of any config file (the registry lookup
#   fails closed). See api-server/src/goose_acp.rs for the rest of the
#   lockdown story.
goose = { git = "https://github.com/block/goose.git", rev = "022c17c3946b506b031fc828543cb9e6650dbfd5", default-features = false }

# roshera-mcp

MCP server exposing the Roshera geometry kernel to agents — the bridge that
makes any MCP client (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, …) a Roshera
client with zero integration work.

## What it provides

**Perception**
- `render_part` — deterministic offscreen render returned as **image
  content** directly in the tool result. `mode: "ids"` paints each B-Rep
  face a distinct flat color and returns the color→face_id legend
  (set-of-marks for topology). `depth` / `normals` are exact G-buffer
  channels.
- `get_pointer` — what the human is pointing at in the viewport (click →
  face id + hover report). Grounds "this face / here" in conversation.
- `get_part`, `get_face`, `mass_properties`, `list_parts` — structured
  inspection (world placement, curvatures, exact inertia).

**Modeling**
- Composite one-call creators: `create_box`, `create_cylinder`,
  `create_plate_with_holes` (explicit coordinates, placement echoed back).
- Sketch primitives for everything else: `create_sketch`,
  `sketch_add_shape`, `sketch_points` (batch — a 96-point gear outline is
  one call), `sketch_extrude`, `plane_from_face` (stack features on faces).
- `delete_part`, `clear_parts`.

## Setup

```sh
cd roshera-mcp && npm install && npm run build
```

Registered for this repo in `.mcp.json` (project scope). Requires the
api-server running on `ROSHERA_URL` (default `http://localhost:8081`).

## Surface modes & the scale funnel

A real CAD surface carries hundreds of operations. Paying context for every
tool on every conversation does not scale — and the worst-case MCP client
(no `list_changed`, no deferred schemas) injects the *entire* exposed surface
each turn. So the **default exposed surface is minimal-complete**, and the long
tail stays reachable at fixed cost through a three-tool funnel.

- **`ROSHERA_MCP_SURFACE=minimal`** *(default)* — the 15 core modeling/perception
  verbs plus the 3 meta-tools = **18 tools, ~4.1k tokens**. Everything else lives
  in the internal table, reachable via the funnel.
- **`ROSHERA_MCP_SURFACE=full`** — restores the full **90-tool** direct exposure
  (**~19.4k tokens**); the meta-tools are omitted since the whole surface is
  present. This is the transition escape hatch, not the recommended default.

**The funnel (fixed ~500-token cost, reaches the whole long tail):**
- `find_tool(intent)` — deterministic ranked search over the registry.
- `describe_tool(name)` — full schema + usage notes on demand.
- `invoke(name, args)` — executes any registry tool, validating args against the
  tool's *own* schema first, so a meta-path call is never less checked than a
  direct call.

Benches optimize attention; they never gate capability — `invoke` reaches
everything, always. (Spec: `2026-07-20-mcp-scale-architecture-design.md`.)

## CI gate — the jig ratchet

`roshera-mcp/**` changes are graded in CI (`mcp-quality` job in
`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). The report card is a permanent invariant, like the
fmt gate. Two graders run:

- **`tools/mcp_budget_gate.py`** *(authoritative)* — speaks minimal MCP stdio to
  the built server on both surfaces and asserts the spec §5 Q5 budgets:
  - minimal live-surface bill **≤ 8000 tokens**,
  - **schema hygiene = 100** — every param in every exposed tool has a
    description (a `const`/single-`enum` discriminant is self-describing),
  - per-tool tokens **≤ 3.5× the full-set median**, except a named allowlist of
    wire-contract-fixed schema-heavies (`revolve`, `assembly_mate`,
    `drill_pattern`). (The spec's starting 2× line false-positives ~10
    legitimately-sized multi-param tools on the current right-skewed surface;
    3.5× isolates exactly the three genuine outliers while staying a live
    ratchet — see the script header for the calibration.)

  Tokens use tiktoken (`o200k_base`) when installable, else the registry's
  `chars/4` estimate. Run it locally with:

  ```sh
  cd roshera-mcp && npm run build && python tools/mcp_budget_gate.py
  ```

- **jig** (github.com/Shodh-Labs/jig) — the upstream MCP report-card grader, run
  best-effort and **non-blocking**: it is not published to PyPI under a
  verifiable name (`pip install jig` resolves to an unrelated git-hook tool), so
  CI attempts the real source, verifies the installed CLI is actually the grader,
  and skips loudly otherwise. The fallback gate above holds the line regardless.

## Known kernel issues surfaced through this API

- `#24` — extruded circles tessellate as ~64 planar strips, not one
  analytic cylinder face (`get_face` on a bore reports `plane`).
- `#26` — `clear_parts` can wedge the model (subsequent extrudes fail
  until server restart); prefer `delete_part` loops meanwhile.
- Part ids renumber after deletion — always re-`list_parts` before
  follow-up deletes (the persistent-ID work, task #11, fixes this class).

# ClientMessage/ServerMessage Protocol Architecture

## ⚠️ IMPORTANT: Protocol vs Transport Distinction

This directory implements the **ClientMessage/ServerMessage protocol**, which is the APPLICATION-LEVEL protocol for client-server communication.

### Key Concepts:
- **Protocol**: ClientMessage/ServerMessage (the message format and structure)
- **Transport**: WebSocket (just the delivery mechanism at `/ws` endpoint)

### DO NOT CONFUSE:
- ❌ "WebSocket protocol" - INCORRECT, WebSocket is just transport
- ✅ "ClientMessage protocol" - CORRECT, this is our actual protocol
- ✅ "ClientMessage sent over WebSocket" - CORRECT and precise

## Architecture Overview

```
┌─────────────┐                              ┌─────────────┐
│   Frontend  │                              │   Backend   │
│             │                              │             │
│  Sends:     │  ----[ WebSocket Transport ]--->  Receives: │
│ClientMessage│         at /ws endpoint       │ClientMessage│
│             │                              │             │
│  Receives:  │  <---[ WebSocket Transport ]----  Sends:    │
│ServerMessage│                              │ServerMessage│
└─────────────┘                              └─────────────┘
```

## Protocol Structure

### ClientMessage (Frontend → Backend)
```rust
pub enum ClientMessage {
    // Authentication
    Authenticate { token: String, request_id: Option<String> },
    
    // Feature-specific commands
    GeometryCommand { command: GeometryWSCommand, request_id: Option<String> },
    TimelineCommand { command: TimelineWSCommand, request_id: Option<String> },
    ExportCommand { command: ExportWSCommand, request_id: Option<String> },
    AICommand { command: AIWSCommand, request_id: Option<String> },
    SessionCommand { command: SessionWSCommand, request_id: Option<String> },
    // ... more variants
}
```

### ServerMessage (Backend → Frontend)
```rust
pub enum ServerMessage {
    Welcome { ... },
    Success { result: Option<Value>, request_id: Option<String> },
    Error { error_code: String, message: String, ... },
    // ... more variants
}
```

## Vision Commands Example

Vision commands are part of the ClientMessage protocol under AICommand:

```rust
ClientMessage::AICommand {
    command: AIWSCommand::ProcessCommandWithVision {
        text: "select the red box",
        viewport: ViewportCapture { ... },
        context: None
    },
    request_id: Some("req_123")
}
```

## File Organization

- `protocol.rs` - Defines ClientMessage/ServerMessage enums and all command types
- `handlers.rs` - Handles incoming ClientMessage and sends ServerMessage responses
- `mod.rs` - Module exports

## For AI Assistants and Developers

When discussing this system:
1. **Always refer to it as "ClientMessage protocol" not "WebSocket protocol"**
2. **WebSocket is just the transport layer, not the protocol**
3. **The protocol is ClientMessage (client→server) and ServerMessage (server→client)**
4. **Vision integration is through ClientMessage::AICommand, not a separate system**

## Common Misconceptions to Avoid

❌ **WRONG**: "The WebSocket handlers process vision commands"
✅ **RIGHT**: "The ClientMessage handlers process vision commands sent over WebSocket"

❌ **WRONG**: "WebSocket protocol includes ProcessCommandWithVision"
✅ **RIGHT**: "ClientMessage protocol includes ProcessCommandWithVision in AICommand"

❌ **WRONG**: "Vision uses a different WebSocket endpoint"
✅ **RIGHT**: "Vision commands use the same ClientMessage protocol at /ws endpoint"
